# Gothic II to OpenGothic save converter

An **experimental, multi-stage migration toolkit** for original Gothic II: Night of the Raven saves and OpenGothic's native save format. This is an ongoing development project, not a finished universal converter.

**Created by an LLM (OpenAI Codex).** New converter code, integration, tests, and documentation were generated by the LLM. The project uses [ZenKit](https://github.com/GothicKit/ZenKit) and [OpenGothic](https://github.com/Try/OpenGothic); their original authorship and licenses remain intact.

The Android graphics work lives separately in [opengothic-android-adreno610](https://github.com/SlopPort/opengothic-android-adreno610). This converter is about save state, not graphics drivers.

## Current status

One original save was migrated with the development prototype, loaded on the tested Android build, saved by the engine, and reloaded. A visible character-stat check and structural checks of the native output were performed. This validates one prototype migration; it does not establish complete save compatibility or prove that every quest can be finished.

The public CLI was extracted from that prototype. A complete run from a clean checkout through a fresh engine migration session is still pending. The device result must not be read as an end-to-end test of this extracted CLI.

The supported workflow currently requires a **manual migration session in the matching engine**. It is not a one-click conversion of an arbitrary save folder. The original save is read by the tools; outputs go into a separate workspace and new save files.

### Implemented scope of the prototype

- Script integer globals/arrays, journal entries, and known-dialog information.
- Player and NPC attributes, talents, inventory, position, and selected equipment state.
- Native world generation followed by offline restoration of loose world items, container contents, container/door locks, and the original guild-attitude table.
- Available enable/count flags of uniquely matched triggers and a subset of uniquely matched movers. Some original animation state is only approximated.
- Calendar/playtime normalization and accessory-equipment pointers without reapplying stat bonuses.
- An optional engine patch that preserves total playtime without retiming the simulation's NPC timers.

### Important limits

- Only a current `NEWWORLD` save with `NEWWORLD` and optional `OLDWORLD` data is supported. Addonworld, other current worlds, Gothic 1, mods, and arbitrary engine versions are unsupported.
- The binary layout is restricted to the tested **OpenGothic format 56** and the pinned [Android fork revision](https://github.com/borsuczyna/OpenGothic-Android/tree/118afdc10d79a7f3357e28c6ee52f6fc2fba8586). A matching format number alone does not establish compatibility with another engine revision.
- Exact AI queues, NPC news, routines, spawn scheduling, all interactions, and all dynamic world relationships are not reproduced. Duplicate or ambiguous object matches are skipped or rejected rather than treated as exact matches.
- Trigger/mover restoration is partial; the full original engine behavior is not emulated. No full-storyline regression test has been performed.
- The tested source text used CP1250. Other text encodings and game editions need validation. The original and migration sessions must use matching game scripts/data.

Keep independent backups. Treat the result as a save for testing, not as the only copy of a playthrough.

## Build the readers

Requirements: a C++20 compiler, CMake 3.22+, Git, and Python 3.10+. ZenKit is fetched at a pinned revision and patched for packed-inventory parsing. No game files are needed to compile the tools.

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --config Release --parallel 4
python -m unittest discover -s tests
```

With a multi-configuration generator, executables may be in `build/Release` instead of `build`.

## Migration workflow

Read [the complete workflow](docs/WORKFLOW.md) before running it. It requires your own game data and a fresh migration session. No personal save, game archive, modified `GOTHIC.DAT`, snapshot, signing key, or compiled game asset is included in this repository.

```sh
python convert.py prepare --game-dir /path/to/Gothic-II --save-dir /path/to/savegame1 --workspace work/session --tools-dir build
# Complete the manual engine session described in docs/WORKFLOW.md.
python convert.py finalize --game-dir /path/to/Gothic-II --workspace work/session --tools-dir build --native-save /path/to/intermediate.sav --output /path/to/converted-test.sav
```

Finalization normalizes the session, restores supported world state, generates any missing item templates from the local DAT, restores accessory pointers, and checks the native structure before publishing the output without overwriting an existing file. It does not certify quest logic or AI correctness. Run Python normally, without `-O`: this prototype still uses assertions for several structural guards.

## Check a native save

No game files or compiled exporters are required for structural validation:

```sh
python convert.py validate --native-save /path/to/converted-test.sav
```

The command checks the pinned format-56 header, session/world/calendar agreement, declared visited-world payloads, explicit contiguous NPC directories, required NPC data/visual entries, item records, and inventory pointers. Empty NPC inventories may be omitted, as in the engine. It checks the active and visited worlds, including their inventories. The JSON report excludes the save title and individual character/item data.

These checks do not decode every NPC field, validate script symbol identities against the game DAT, certify a different engine revision, or prove quest/AI behavior. The finalizer applies these checks to both its native input and completed candidate.

## Development

[ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) lists the next steps. [Format notes](docs/FORMAT.md) document the layout assumptions and a critical directory-entry requirement. [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) covers attribution and licenses.

Bug reports should use synthetic/minimal fixtures where possible. Original saves and decoded snapshots can contain personal playthrough details; do not attach them publicly by default. The optional diagnostic network listener is **off by default** and uses a generated per-workspace token when explicitly enabled.

This is an unofficial project, independent of the Gothic rights holders and upstream engine maintainers.
